Where it began

Sai Sudharsan grew up in a sporting home. His father represented India in athletics at the South Asian Games in Dhaka, and his mother played volleyball at state level, so there was never much doubt that he would end up playing something.

Cricket won. In 2018 he was at the youth academy of Chennai Super Kings, and in the 2019-20 season he was the leading run-scorer for Alwarpet CC in Chennai club cricket, with 635 runs at 52.92. His runs in the Tamil Nadu Premier League earned him an IPL place, and in the 2021-22 season he made his first appearances for Tamil Nadu in the short formats.

The player

Gujarat Titans signed him for the 2022 IPL. In the 2023 final against Chennai Super Kings he made 96, and in 2024 he was his side's top scorer with 527 runs. Then in 2025 he made 759 runs at 54.21 and won the Orange Cap for the season's leading run-scorer.

He made 127 runs, with two fifties, in his first one-day series for India, against South Africa in December 2023, and his Test debut came in the first Test of the series against England in June 2025. By November 2026 he had played seven Tests, scoring 383 runs at 31.92 with three fifties and a best of 87, and holding six catches.

What made him special

Consistency, mostly. That Orange Cap made him, in 2025, the youngest winner of the award and the youngest batter to pass 700 runs in an IPL season. With Shubman Gill at the other end he formed an opening pair that became the first in men's T20 cricket to share eleven century partnerships. A spell with Surrey in the County Championship in 2023 also gave him a taste of English cricket two years before he first played a Test against England.

The one thing missing by November 2026 was a first Test hundred, though 87 showed he was not far off.

And finally

He does seem to like keeping people waiting for his hundreds: 96 in an IPL final, 87 in a Test. When one does arrive it can come in a hurry, though. His hundred against Chennai in 2024 took him just 59 balls.
